claims.text: A thin molybdenum interlayer can be used between tungsten and CuCrZr.
A Mo interlayer reduces thermal-expansion mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
A Mo interlayer limits interfacial diffusion in W/CuCrZr joints.
Reducing thermal-expansion mismatch and interfacial diffusion enhances joint mechanical stability under fusion-reactor conditions.
The proposed starting materials are high-purity W and CuCrZr substrates with native surface states.
The Mo interlayer may be introduced by deposition or bonding at the W/CuCrZr interface.
The intended service conditions include high temperature, rapid thermal cycling, and irradiation representative of fusion reactors.
Mo provides an intermediate transition between the thermal-expansion characteristics of W and CuCrZr.
Molybdenum has an intermediate thermal-expansion coefficient relative to W and CuCrZr.
The Mo layer acts as a diffusion barrier and stress-relief layer.
The Mo layer promotes a stable interfacial microstructure that minimizes thermally induced crack initiation and propagation.
Compared with direct W/CuCrZr joints, Mo-interlayer joints will have improved interfacial adhesion.
Compared with direct W/CuCrZr joints, Mo-interlayer joints will exhibit less microstructural degradation and interfacial cracking.
Directly bonded W/CuCrZr joints are prone to cracking and diffusion-related failure under thermal stress.
The effectiveness of the Mo interlayer depends on layer thickness, deposition method, irradiation exposure, and operating-temperature regime.
